question: The National Liberal Party was a liberal party of the North German Confederation and the German Empire?
The National Liberal Party flourished between 1867 and 1918?
The National Liberals became the dominant party in the Reichstag during the Prussian-led unification of Germany?
The National Liberals contained two wings reflecting conflicting claims of its Hegelian and idealistic heritage?
One wing of the National Liberals emphasized the power of the state through the Nationalstaat?
The other wing of the National Liberals emphasized the civil liberties of the Rechtsstaat?
The cleavage between the two wings later proved fatal for the unity of the National Liberals?
The National Liberals managed to remain the pivotal party in the decades after unification by cooperating with both the Progressives and the Free Conservatives on various issues?

A first national liberal parliamentary group arose among right-wing deputies of the liberal German Progress Party in the Prussian House of Representatives during a constitutional conflict sparked by Minister President Otto von Bismarck?
In 1862, Otto von Bismarck overruled the Liberal opposition in parliament using the so-called Lückentheorie ("Gap Theory") to justify proceeding with taxes for military reforms of the Prussian Army?
Otto von Bismarck delivered a martial "Blood and Iron" speech in 1862?
Otto von Bismarck aimed to reconcile with his opponents by strengthening Prussian hegemony, which culminated in the Seven Weeks' War of 1866?
The National Liberals supported Bismarck's highly successful foreign policy after the victory over the Austrian forces at the Battle of Königgrätz on 3 July?
Bismarck introduced a bill that formalized his circumvention of parliamentary budgetary rights after the victory at the Battle of Königgrätz?
At voting time on 3 September, 19 National Liberal deputies opted for Bismarck's Indemnity Law?
The Liberals who opposed the Indemnity Law argued that Bismarck was asking them to compromise on constitutional government?
The supporters of the Indemnity Law believed opposition was fruitless because Bismarck had the firm support of King Wilhelm I?
The supporters of the Indemnity Law believed that accepting the bill would put them in a better position to press for greater freedom?
The first National Liberal faction in the Prussian parliament was formed on 17 November around Eduard Lasker and Hans Victor von Unruh?
The National Liberal Party was founded in the course of the North German federal election held on 12 February 1867?
The National Liberals gathered support from the Prussian annexed territories of Hanover and Hesse-Nassau as well as from the other states of the Confederation?
The National Liberals emerged as the largest faction in the North German Reichstag?
An inaugural declaration was adopted by the National Liberals on 12 June?
The first party chairman of the National Liberal Party was Rudolf von Bennigsen?
The National Liberals strongly advocated the interests of the Grand Burgher (German: Großbürger) dynasties and business magnates?
The National Liberals also advocated the interests of nationalist-minded Protestant circles of the educated bourgeoisie (Bildungsbürgertum)?
The key points of the National Liberal party manifesto focused on national unification and Bismarck's policies?
The National Liberals' period of great dominance was between 1871 and 1879?
During this period, the National Liberals were Bismarck's chief allies in the Reichstag?
The National Liberals were avid supporters of the anti-Catholic Kulturkampf measures and the Anti-Socialist Laws?
In the first all-German federal election held on 3 March 1871, the National Liberals reached 30.1% of the votes?
The National Liberals became the strongest group in the Reichstag parliament with 119 seats in 1871?
The Reichstag faction remained the political centre of power as the National Liberals never attained a large number of members?
Rudolf von Bennigsen was the chairman of the National Liberal Party?
The stabilization of the new state was feasible because of the National Liberals' support as de facto ruling party?
The National Liberals guided Bismarck's domestic policies, especially in regards to national economics and the legal foundations of the German Empire?
Weights and measurements were standardized by the National Liberals?
A common German market was created by the National Liberals?
A national bank, the Reichsbank, was created by the National Liberals?
Numerous regional currencies were replaced with the Goldmark by the National Liberals?
The liberal economic policies laid the groundworks for the economic boom the German nation experienced at the turn of the 19th century?
In 1879, Bismarck's alliance with the National Liberals broke over his abandonment of free trade by the adoption of a tariff?
In the economic crisis following the Panic of 1873, several lobbying associations exerted pressure on Bismarck who increasingly favoured a more protectionist approach?
The shift to protectionism violated the liberal principles of both the National Liberals and the more left-leaning liberal German Progress Party?
The shift to protectionism has been characterized as Bismarck's conservative turn?
This shift meant an enduring shift of the Chancellor to the right?
This shift changed the political climate of the fledgling nation and soured relations between Bismarck and a number of leading German liberals?
The National Liberals lost their status as the dominant party in 1880?
The left-wing represented by the Liberal Union split off and merged with the Progress Party into the German Free-minded Party by 1884?
The remaining partisans of the National Liberals approached the Conservatives?
The Conservatives became the strongest supporters of Alfred von Tirpitz's various Fleet Acts starting in 1898?
The Fleet Acts pushed Great Britain into an arms race with Germany until World War I?
In the federal election of 1887, a right-wing cartel of National Liberals, Conservatives and Free Conservatives ensured a parliamentary majority for Bismarck until his resignation in 1890?
Bismarck deserted the liberals and came to terms with a new less confrontational Pope during the Kulturkampf?
Bismarck started working politically with the Catholic Centre Party during the Kulturkampf?
Historian Hajo Holborn examines the contradictions between the Kulturkampf and liberal values?
David Blackbourn says the liberal attacks on the Catholic Church left a political legacy that was the opposite of what liberals wanted?
David Blackbourn says the liberal attacks on the Catholic Church made liberals beholden to Bismarck?
David Blackbourn says the liberal attacks on the Catholic Church helped consolidate political Catholicism in Germany?
In 1905, Ernst Bassermann became chairman of the National Liberal Party?
Ernst Bassermann followed chairman Johannes von Miquel?
The National Liberals came to be closely associated with the interests of big business?
The National Liberals maintained strong relations with mighty industrialist advocacy groups?
The National Liberals maintained strong relations with imperialist and nationalist associations like the Pan-German League?
The National Liberals became more conservative as they were increasingly threatened by the growing strength of the Social Democrats?
The National Liberal Party was generally split between a more liberal wing that sought to strengthen ties with the dissident liberals to their left?
The National Liberal Party had a right-wing that came to support more protectionist policies and close relations with the Conservatives and the imperial government?
During World War I, most of the National Liberals, including such leaders of their left wing as Gustav Stresemann, avidly supported the expansionist goals of the imperial government?
The National Liberals also called for reform at home during World War I?
Following the war, the National Liberal Party broke up?
Gustav Stresemann led the main body of the National Liberal Party, including most of its moderate and conservative elements, into the conservative liberal German People's Party?
The left wing of the National Liberals merged with the left-liberal Progressive People's Party to form the German Democratic Party?
The far-right wing of the National Liberals joined the German National People's Party?
